LanguageData.RC2_DriedFruit.label: dried fruit
LanguageData.RC2_DriedFruit.description: Fruit that has been dried, often near a fire, in the sun, or in an oven. With its moisture gone, they last quite a bit longer and travel well. Favored by caravneers and tribals alike. Can be used in cooking recipes.
LanguageData.RC2_DriedMeat.label: dried meat
LanguageData.RC2_DriedMeat.description: Meat hunks that have been trimmed of most, if not all, of their fat and dried near a fire or in a stove. Dried meat travels well and lasts quite a bit longer than raw meat. Favored by tribals and caravaneers. Can be eaten by itself without issue, but is often used in cooking recipes, especially stews, to soften it up.
LanguageData.RC2_Hardtack.label: hardtack
LanguageData.RC2_Hardtack.description: A tough biscuit or cracker that lasts a very long time and is good for travelling. Makes you thirsty and doesn't taste very good though.
LanguageData.RC2_PickleBrine.label: brined vegetables
LanguageData.RC2_PickleBrine.description: Vegetables that have been trimmed of excess leafage and mixed in with a briney solution, ready for long-term pickling in a barrel.
LanguageData.RC2_PickledVegetables.label: pickled vegetables
LanguageData.RC2_PickledVegetables.description: Vegetables that have been packed into a jar or can with a briny or vinegary solution. Favored by those with a taste for vinegar, they're also often used in cooking and they last a long time.
LanguageData.RC2_PreparedFruit.label: prepared fruit
LanguageData.RC2_PreparedFruit.description: Fruit that has been peeled, slice, and/or de-pitted/seeded so it can easily be dried.
LanguageData.RC2_TrimmedMeat.label: trimmed meat
LanguageData.RC2_TrimmedMeat.description: Meat hunks that have been trimmed of most, if not all, of their fat and ready to be dried at a drying rack.
